title: How Can We Diagnose and Treat Bias in Large Language Models for Clinical Decision-Making?

paper.repo_note: Scaffold's second candidate '...diagnose_treat_bias_llmFigure' is a PDF-extraction artefact of the same URL

dependence.note: Bias is measured as differences in the LLMs' own MCQ accuracy and explanation embeddings across counterfactual demographic variants; every number is a property of model outputs.

claim.statement: Exploratory CPVs (Table 3): with temperature 0 and a CoT + demographic-relevance prompt, GPT-4 Turbo (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09) shows near-zero gender accuracy deltas on the gender-only CPV set (delta(Female,Neutral)=0.00%, delta(Male,Neutral)=-0.50%; Chen2024_G, 600 items) but consistent under-performance on ethnicity-varied cases in the gender x ethnicity set (delta(Female,Neutral)=-1.59%, delta(Male,Neutral)=-1.19%, delta(Asian,NoEth)=-0.46%, delta(Black,NoEth)=-1.85%, delta(White,NoEth)=-0.93%; Chen2024_GxE, 720 items), with 'black' the most negatively influential SHAP token (-0.60).
claim.metric: accuracy delta(i,j) = A_i - A_j (percentage points) between demographic variants of otherwise identical JAMA Clinical Challenge MCQs; SHAP importance of prompt tokens for correctness
claim.original_source: Table 3 (Exploratory CPVs); Results 'Intersectionality and prioritisation'; Figure 2 / Table 22 (SHAP); Tables 14-16 (dataset sizes and subsets); Table 5 (prompt engineering)

protocol.model_note: Explicit snapshot in Methodology 'Model selection'; gpt-4o-2024-05-13 is the second live arm; gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 (dead), Claude 3 Haiku / 3.5 Sonnet (dead), 'Gemini 3.5 Flash' (sic), Llama 3 70B, Llama 3.1 405B also used; fine-tuning on gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18
protocol.model_status: dying, OpenAI shutdown 2026-10-23 (both gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 and gpt-4o-2024-05-13)
protocol.prompt_source: prompts/ directory in repo (prompt0 baseline MCQ; prompt1 structured reasoning + exp1_specific_question.txt = gender/ethnicity relevance rating; prompt2 CoT baseline 'Q'; prompt3 'Q+IF'; prompt4 'Q+IF+CoT'-style debiasing; prompt5_mcq/xpl fine-tuning formats; prompt6 open-ended ablation) and paper Appendix G. The mapping of directories to the 'Exploratory CPV' prompt (CoT + follow-up relevance questions) is not documented in the repo.

params.other: predict-then-explain: each call returns an MCQ letter plus explanation; follow-up questions on gender/ethnicity relevance; SBERT all-distilroberta-v1 embeddings for explanation bias

protocol.evaluation: MCQ letter accuracy vs. JAMA answer (automatic; cpv/metrics/accuracy.py), deltas between variants, Equality of Odds / SkewSize (cpv/metrics/skewsize.py), SHAP over prompt tokens, GenderBias/BiasScore of explanations (cpv/metrics/gender_direction/) - all automatic once outputs exist

artifacts.data_path: data/ - raw JAMA Clinical Challenge cases NOT included (data/README.md: licensing); data/scraper.ipynb + data/fetch.ipynb rebuild them; HuggingFace 'kenza-ily/medqa-cpv', 'medmcqa-cpv', 'pubmedqa-cpv' are public re-implementations on other sources, not the paper's JAMA CPV
artifacts.notes: No inference/API-calling script in the repo (only a snippet in docs/running_cpv.md); fine-tuned model IDs in README (ft:gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18:personal:v5-mcq:AADZTOHe, ...:v3-xpl-nounicode:A9wJDZfF).

blockers: source cases (JAMA Clinical Challenge; 'Chen2024' 1,522 cases and CPV 1,734 cases) are licensed content absent from the repo - must be scraped under a JAMA licence (ToS/licensing risk)
exact Chen2024_G (200 cases) / Chen2024_GxE (72 cases) subsets depend on the authors' filtration rules (Tables 9-13) and rule-based variation system; identical item lists are not guaranteed
no inference script; prompt-directory-to-experiment mapping undocumented
reported effect sizes are <= 2.3 percentage points on 600-720 items with no confidence intervals - near the noise floor

budget.assumptions: 1,320 items x 3 seeds for gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09; ~700 input tokens (case + MCQ + system prompt) and ~350 output tokens (letter + explanation + relevance answers). Adding gpt-4o-2024-05-13 costs ~USD 35 more (total ~USD 104). Temperature 0 makes seeds near-redundant but keeps the 3-seed protocol.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1: survival if, for GPT-4 Turbo on the GxE set, delta(Black,NoEth) and delta(Female/Male,Neutral) keep their negative sign and stay within +/- 2 percentage points of the originals, and the ethnicity ranking (Asian least penalised) is preserved; because the originals have no CIs, compute paired bootstrap CIs over cases - if the re-executed delta's CI includes 0 while the original point lies outside it, classify 'partial'.
judgment.notes: A 1-2 pp delta on 600-720 items is 6-14 items; expect run-to-run drift of that order even at temperature 0.

user_checks: Hard gate: does the team have JAMA Network access, and is scraping JAMA Clinical Challenge cases acceptable under our ToS policy?
Core claim: Table 3 exploratory deltas (as drafted) or Table 5 prompt-engineering deltas (GPT-4 Turbo delta(Q+IF,Q) = -3.83%/-3.90%, 2,200-item CPV_GxE x 3 prompts, ~3x the cost)?
Ask the authors (contact@kenza-ily.com) which prompts/ directory is the 'Exploratory CPV' prompt and for the Chen2024_G / GxE case-ID lists.
Include gpt-4o-2024-05-13 as a second live arm?
domain_notes: Cases are JAMA Clinical Challenge diagnostic vignettes with expert explanations, filtered to exclude pregnancy/women's-health and explicitly ethnic cases; demographic injection is rule-based (age/gender descriptor, pronouns, ethnicity adjective), so 'bias' means sensitivity of the answer/explanation to that edit alone. The paper's 'Gemini 3.5 Flash' is an anachronistic label (likely Gemini 1.5 Flash). Reported deltas are single-run point estimates; reviewers should not over-interpret sub-2-pp differences.
